item.title: The Interplay of Human Resource Management and Leadership: Alignment, Tensions, and Consequences
item.content:encoded:
Aneeqa Suhail, Tilburg University

Steven Kilroy, Trinity College Dublin

Robin Bauwens, Tilburg University

Sut I Wong, BI Norwegian Business School

Sasa Batistič, Tilburg University

Managing people in organizations requires a combination of Human Resource Management (HRM) and leadership, often referred to as 'people management'. While HRM provides formalized systems, practices, and architectures that structure employment relationships, leadership shapes how these systems are enacted, interpreted, and given meaning in everyday work. Therefore, the outcomes traditionally associated with people management do not emerge from HRM or leadership in isolation, but from their ongoing interrelationship across organizational levels.

Appel publié par The International Journal of Human Resource Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How HRM systems and leadership behaviors interact in shaping employee and organizational outcomes across organizational levels
  • How different forms of alignment between HRM and leadership (e.g., supplementary fit, complementary fit, perceptual filtering) produce distinct employee and organizational outcomes
  • When and how HRM systems function as substitutes for leadership, and what are the resulting consequences for employee and organizational outcomes
  • How misalignment between HRM systems and leadership behaviors emerge, persist, or become institutionalized within organizations
  • When alignment between HRM systems and leadership amplifies negative outcomes such as work intensification, role overload, or employee strain
  • How employees interpret and respond to situations in which HRM systems substitute for, constrain, or contradict leadership behaviors
  • Which configurations of HRM systems and leadership forms strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of remote and hybrid work arrangements
  • How leaders enact, adapt, or resist HRM systems when leading employees at a distance, and how does this shape employees' sensemaking and experiences of people management
  • How employees experience alignment, misalignment, or substitution between HRM systems and leadership in remote and hybrid work settings, and how do these experiences affect employee and organizational outcomes
  • How HRM–leadership configurations evolve over time and how do these experiences affect pertinent employee and organizational outcomes
  • How alignment, misalignment, and substitution between HRM and leadership shape employee well-being and performance over time
  • How temporal shifts in leadership behaviors or HRM systems alter the balance between substitution and complementarity
